blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Authorities have issued a public health warning after shellfish samples collected off San Benito town in Surigao del Norte tested positive for paralytic shellfish poison, commonly known as red tide toxins. In an advisory, the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) in Caraga region said laboratory screening using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay detected toxic levels in shellfish meat taken from the coastal municipality. While confirmatory tests remain underway, BFAR urged the public as a precautionary measure to refrain from harvesting, selling, buying and eating all types of shellfish and Acetes (shrimp that looks like krill)—locally […]...
